title: GOALS-JWST: resolved multiphase molecular gas in IRAS 20551-4250 using JWST and ALMA
question: Investigate the nature of the nuclear regions in IRAS 20551-4250, characterise cold and warm molecular gas properties, and infer whether the molecular gas observations provide evidence of feedback from starburst or AGN.

data.angular_resolution: array angular resolution ~0.06 arcsec (TM1) and ~0.26 arcsec (TM2); synthesized beam 0.12x0.10 arcsec^2; smoothed to 0.8 arcsec
data.sensitivity: 0.44 mJy/beam per 4.5 km s^-1 channel (in dirty cube)

what.value: Warm molecular gas masses for a comparison sub-sample of GOALS ULIRGs derived from Spitzer/IRS spectra.

evidence.quote: The warm molecular gas masses presented in Fig. 15 are taken from (cite: petric18), based on a sub-sample of the parent GOALS galaxies from where IR20551 was selected.

what.value: Cold molecular gas masses for the comparison ULIRG sample drawn from integrated CARMA CO(1-0) observations.

evidence.quote: The cold molecular gas masses are drawn from integrated CARMA CO(1–0) observations (cite: alatalo24), who assume an $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ value of 1.5, comparable to the value of 1.8 used in this paper for IR20551.

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA CO(2-1) cube and match resolution to JWST/MIRI-MRS
recipe.method: Recreate calibrated MSs via CASA pipeline, isolate CO(2-1) spectral window, subtract 0th-order continuum with uvcontsub, image both configurations jointly in 4.5 km/s channels with tclean using Briggs robust=2.0, multi-scale then hogbom cleaning, apply primary beam correction, smooth to 0.8 arcsec Gaussian beam and re-grid to MRS.
key_parameters: channel width = 4.5 km s^-1, robust = 2.0, multiscale scales = [0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 3.0] arcsec, smoothed beam = 0.8 arcsec

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST/MIRI-MRS IFU data and extract nuclear and integrated spectra
recipe.method: Run 3-stage JWST pipeline with CRDS context jwst_1256.pmap, cosmic ray shower finding, sigma-clipping of warm pixels on rate files, residual fringe correction, dedicated background subtraction, and pixel_replace; extract R = 0.5 and 1.5 arcsec aperture spectra and stitch continuum across channels.
key_parameters: CRDS = jwst_1256.pmap, find_showers = True, skip_residual_fringe = FALSE, outlier threshold = 99%, pixel_replace = True, aperture radii = 0.5 and 1.5 arcsec

recipe.goal: Model mid-infrared continuum and warm H2 rotational lines S(1)-S(8)
recipe.method: Model overall mid-IR continuum, PAH emission, and silicate absorption with CAFE; subtract continuum and fit H2 0-0 S(1)-S(8) lines with single Gaussians within +/-0.03 um windows in aperture spectra and spaxel-by-spaxel; apply CAFE extinction corrections and instrumental LSF corrections.
key_parameters: spectral window = +/-0.03 um around line centre, 100 Monte Carlo mock spectra for uncertainties

recipe.goal: Fit ALMA CO(2-1) emission line profiles and derive non-parametric kinematics
recipe.method: Extract R = 1.5 arcsec integrated spectrum and spaxel-by-spaxel spectra from ALMA CO(2-1) cube, fit up to two Gaussians selected by BIC, and compute non-parametric v_50, w_80, and total flux.

recipe.goal: Model VLT/MUSE optical spectra, construct BPT maps, and measure ionised outflow rate
recipe.method: Subtract stellar continuum using ppxf within LZIFU, fit optical emission lines (Hbeta, [O III]5007, Halpha, [N II]6585, [O I]6300, [S II]6716,6731) with up to 2 Gaussians plus linear continuum, construct [N II] and [O I] BPT maps, compute [O III] v_50 and w_80, and derive ionised gas mass outflow rate.
key_parameters: aperture radius = 1.5 arcsec, maximum Gaussians = 2, [O III]5007:[O III]4959 = 3:1
assumptions: Solar metallicity of the gas; broad Gaussian component represents outflowing gas

recipe.goal: Derive warm H2 excitation temperatures and warm molecular gas mass
recipe.method: Construct H2 rotational excitation diagrams from extinction-corrected S(1)-S(8) fluxes in nuclear and integrated apertures and spaxel-by-spaxel; fit two-temperature linear models to excitation diagrams and a continuous power-law temperature distribution (Togi & Smith 2016) to derive warm H2 mass at T >= 200 K.
key_parameters: upper temperature bound = 2000 K, lower integration temperature = 200 K, aperture R = 1.5 arcsec
assumptions: Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE) and ortho-para ratio of 3:1

recipe.goal: Calculate cold molecular gas mass from ALMA CO(2-1) and compare cold-to-warm gas ratios
recipe.method: Calculate CO(2-1) luminosity L'_CO(2-1) within R = 1.5 arcsec using Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005) equation, convert to cold H2 mass using excitation correction r_21 and alpha_CO, and compute integrated and spatially resolved (convolved/rebinned) CO(2-1)/H2 S(2) ratios.
assumptions: CO excitation ratio r_21 = 0.4, alpha_CO = 1.8 M_sun K^-1 km^-1 s pc^-2, H0 = 70 km s^-1, Omega_M = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7

evidence.quote: From the integrated CO transition shown in Fig. 6, we find $L^{\prime}_{\rm CO(2-1)} = 2.8\times10^{9}$ K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$.
